perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- He knows he is a construction worker and Elizabeth is the receptionist at the same company; they have a friendly but professional relationship.
- He observed Elizabeth being unusually curt with him over the past few days.
- He asked if he had upset her. Elizabeth said no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and apologized if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic and offered to listen or take a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted and thanked him.
- Over coffee, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses; Keith perceived them as quite severe.
- He suggested she consider talking to a professional. Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was hesitant/unsure.
- He noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn after his suggestion. He believed he might have embarrassed her, regretted it, and reassured her that he did not mean to overstep and was there to support her.
- Elizabeth told him he did not overstep, that she appreciated his concern, and that it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative. She thanked him, said his support meant a lot to her, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith believes Elizabeth values his support and feels more comfortable around him now. He intends to maintain this supportive relationship.
